Maidstone's population increased by around 20,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 180,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Maidstone increased by 13.3%, from around 155,100 in 2011 to around 175,800 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Maidstone was home to around 3.2 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 2.8 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 40% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Maidstone than across the South East

Median age stable in Maidstone

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 41 years in Maidstone between the last two censuses.

This area had a similar average (median) age to the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 4,600 (an increase of 15.6%), while the number of residents between 16 and 19 years fell by around 450 (6.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Maidstone stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Maidstone, but fell across England.

In Maidstone, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 12.7% in 2011 to 13.4% in 2021, while across England it fell from 17.7% to 17.1%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 13.7% to 13.6%.

Private renting in Maidstone increased from 14.6% to 17.3%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 70.5% to 67.4%.

The rate of social renting in Maidstone increased by 0.6 percentage points

Maidstone residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 148,300 Maidstone residents said they were born in England. This represented 84.3% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 137,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 88.6% of Maidstone's population.

Countries that joined the EU between April 2001 and March 2011 (other than Poland, Croatia, Lithuania and Romania) were the next most represented, with around 2,800 Maidstone residents reporting one of these countries as their country of birth (1.6%). This figure was up from around 1,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.7% of the population of Maidstone.

The number of Maidstone residents born in Poland rose from around 1,500 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to just under 2,300 in 2021 (1.3%).

In 2021, 84.3% of Maidstone residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Maidstone

In 2021, 8.4% of Maidstone residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 5.8% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.6% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Maidstone that identified as "British only" increased from 15.0% to 55.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Maidstone (2.6 percentage points) than across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Maidstone increased by 2.6 percentage points

Unpaid care in Maidstone

In 2021, 4.5% of Maidstone residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Maidstone (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Maidstone decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Religion in Maidstone

In 2021, 40.1% of Maidstone residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.7% in 2011. The rise of 13.4 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Maidstone. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 49.3% of people in Maidstone described themselves as Christian (down from 62.9%), while 5.7% did not state their religion (down from 7.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Maidstone (3.7 percentage points) than in nearby Tunbridge Wells (0.8 percentage points).

In Maidstone, the percentage of adults who had never been married or in a civil partnership increased from 29.9% in 2011 to 33.7% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Tunbridge Wells increased from 31.3% to 32.1%.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in Maidstone fell from 51.4% to 48.7%, while the percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.1% to 9.4%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Maidstone increased by 3.7 percentage points

Health in Maidstone

In 2021, 49.2% of Maidstone residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 46.7% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.5% to 34.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Maidstone residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.0%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.6% to 3.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

In 2021, 1.0% of usual residents said their health was very bad in Maidstone

Fewer couples without children

Of Maidstone households, 17.6% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 20.2% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Maidstone (2.5 percentage points) than across the South East (1.4 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.4%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Maidstone decreased by 2.5 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Maidstone residents aged 16 years and over, 59.6% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 60.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.3%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.1% in 2011. The percentage of retired Maidstone residents increased from 22.0% to 22.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed in Maidstone (1.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.3 percentage points, from 59.0% to 57.6%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Maidstone decreased by 1.1 percentage points

Working hours in Maidstone

In 2021, 10.1% of Maidstone residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (10.0%).

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 10.4% to 11.0% across the South East. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Maidstone increased by 0.1 percentage points

Disability in Maidstone

In 2021, 6.3% of Maidstone residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.8%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.4% in 2011. The proportion of Maidstone residents who were not disabled increased from 83.2% to 83.8%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Maidstone (1.0 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Maidstone decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Maidstone

In 2021, 4.7% of Maidstone residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 3.2% in 2011. The 1.5 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 89.8% of people in Maidstone identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 94.1% in 2011), while 2.3% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.9% in 2011 to 2.1% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
